skill.name: scaffolding-openai-agents
skill.description: Guides developers through building OpenAI Agents SDK applications with async runners, tools, handoffs, guardrails, streaming, tracing, and FastAPI integration.
skill.summary: Scaffold OpenAI Agents SDK projects with practical async, tool, guardrail, and orchestration patterns.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, placeholder setup commands, benign documentation URLs, and simple verification text. One confirmed high-risk issue remains: the skill demonstrates eval(expression) inside a function tool, which can teach unsafe dynamic code execution.

remediation.issue: Unsafe eval example in calculator tool
remediation.suggestion: Replace eval(expression) with a constrained arithmetic parser or remove the calculator example. Do not present eval as usable sample code, even with a production warning.

remediation.issue: Network tool example lacks input and error handling guidance
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to validate city input, set request timeouts, and handle HTTP errors when demonstrating external API tools.

content.value_statement: Developers need repeatable patterns for OpenAI Agents SDK applications. This skill provides practical scaffolding for agents, tools, handoffs, guardrails, streaming, and FastAPI integration.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to create basic OpenAI Agents SDK agents with model settings.
Demonstrates Runner patterns for async, sync, streaming, and continued conversations.
Provides examples for function tools, typed tool inputs, and async HTTP tools.
Explains multi-agent handoffs and agents used as tools for orchestration.
Includes guardrail examples for input validation and output validation.
Outlines FastAPI integration and tracing configuration for agent workflows.
limitations: It targets the OpenAI Agents SDK and does not cover LangChain or raw OpenAI API projects.
Some examples are educational and need production hardening before deployment.
It does not provide a complete generated repository or dependency lockfile.
It assumes Python familiarity and basic async programming knowledge.

use_cases.title: Prototype tutoring agents
use_cases.description: Build a Python tutor with specialist agents for concepts, debugging, and exercises.

use_cases.title: Add tool calling to an assistant
use_cases.description: Create function tools for calculations, documentation search, weather lookup, or internal workflow helpers.

use_cases.title: Design multi-agent workflows
use_cases.description: Route requests across specialist agents and coordinate research or writing tasks with manager agents.

prompt_templates.title: Create a simple agent
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a first OpenAI Agents SDK script.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to scaffold a minimal OpenAI Agents SDK Python tutor. Include setup steps, the Agent definition, and an async Runner example.

prompt_templates.title: Add tool calling
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to add a typed function tool to my OpenAI Agents SDK assistant. Show safe input validation and how Runner invokes the agent.

prompt_templates.title: Build handoff routing
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a triage agent that hands off questions to three specialist agents. Include clear handoff descriptions and test prompts.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a production API
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline a FastAPI service around OpenAI Agents SDK with streaming responses, guardrails, tracing, and error handling boundaries.

output_examples.input: Scaffold a Python tutor agent with OpenAI Agents SDK.
output_examples.output: A concise project outline with setup steps, an Agent definition, an async Runner flow, and a short manual test plan.

output_examples.input: Add specialist handoffs for concepts, debugging, and exercises.
output_examples.output: A triage design that names each specialist, explains routing criteria, and describes prompts for verifying each handoff path.

output_examples.input: Prepare this agent for a FastAPI endpoint.
output_examples.output: A service integration plan covering request models, response models, streaming behavior, tracing, and guardrail placement.

best_practices: Use async Runner patterns for application code that may call tools or external services.
Define narrow function tools with typed inputs and explicit validation at boundaries.
Add guardrails for user input and model output before deploying agent workflows.
anti_patterns: Do not run arbitrary expressions or code from model output or user input.
Do not build handoff agents without clear routing descriptions and test cases.
Do not expose raw exception details from production API endpoints.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps build Python applications with the OpenAI Agents SDK, including agents, tools, handoffs, guardrails, streaming, and API integration.

faq.question: Does it support Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools for using the skill guidance.

faq.question: Is this for raw OpenAI API usage?
faq.answer: No. It is focused on the OpenAI Agents SDK and its Agent, Runner, tool, handoff, and guardrail patterns.

faq.question: Can I use the examples in production?
faq.answer: Use them as starting points. Review security, validation, error handling, secrets management, and deployment settings before production use.

faq.question: Does it cover multi-agent systems?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes handoffs for routing and agents-as-tools patterns for orchestrating specialist agents.

faq.question: What security concern should I fix first?
faq.answer: Replace the eval-based calculator example with a safe arithmetic parser or remove it entirely before publishing.
